title: Feature panel: edit any field in one step and act on its flags in place
subtitle: Mock-ups for the roadmap and PRD review: no Change, Save or Cancel per field; flags fixed where they show. Brightwell and its people are made up.

decisions.name: How a field is edited
decisions.question: How should a person change a field in the feature panel?
decisions.common: One panel for every feature (opened here from the Roadmap). The fields the panel has today all stay: the main ones in view, and outcome, notes, horizon, track, PRD, reading, near, why, open decisions and tasks under More (see PE2). Each change saves on its own with an Undo in the corner, Oracle's suggestions can be used or kept aside, and a viewer sees the same panel as plain text, with the flags' words but no buttons. The panel keeps today's 'Code None · Not in the Ground Truth' line. A feature is added from + Add under Depends on or Needed by and is placed by that link, with no drag; a milestone is added at the foot of the Milestone list, and the '+ Milestone' hint on the time axis stays for a milestone with no feature yet. Story in every proposal: move the end date to Dec 4 (the Roadmap bar moves at once), act on a flag, then add a feature.

proposals.name: Edit in place
proposals.what: Every value is already a field: a thin dashed line under it at rest, a box on hover. Click it (or Tab to it), type or pick, and it saves when you leave the field or press Enter; Esc puts the old value back. Lists such as Owner or Milestone open on one click and save on the pick. A new milestone or a new feature is typed straight into its list.
proposals.why: It removes the Change link, the Save button and the Cancel button at once: each common task drops to one or two clicks, and the panel still reads as a list, so nothing new to learn. The dashed line tells at a glance what can be changed, which the brief asks for.
proposals.plus: Fewest clicks with the mouse; works with Tab and Enter too; nothing to remember.
proposals.cost: Add a feature 1 click (+ Add, type, Enter: placed by its link, no drag); move its dates 1 click; set its owner 2 clicks (1 when Oracle suggests someone); add a milestone 2 clicks. Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. The dashed lines add some texture to the panel.

proposals.name: Click to edit
proposals.what: Values read as plain text, like today without the Change links; hovering a value shows a box and a small pencil. One click turns that value into a field; it saves on Enter, on leaving it or on the pick, with no Save button.
proposals.plus: The quietest panel to read; the same click counts as A.
proposals.cost: Add a feature 1 click; move its dates 1 click; set its owner 2 clicks; add a milestone 2 clicks. Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. Nothing shows what can be changed until the pointer is on it, so on a phone (no hover) a person must guess.

proposals.name: One Edit mode
proposals.what: The panel reads as plain text until Edit is pressed; then every field turns into a box at once, and Done saves all the changes together, with one Undo for the lot.
proposals.plus: A clear line between reading and changing; several changes can be made and checked before they count, which suits a review meeting.
proposals.cost: Add a feature 3 clicks; move its dates 3 clicks (Edit, Ends, Done); set its owner 4 clicks; add a milestone 4 clicks. Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. Only the Save step is renamed Done; a change is lost if the panel is closed before Done.

proposals.name: Keyboard first
proposals.what: A line at the top takes a typed change (owner Mira, ends Dec 4), and each common field has a letter: E opens Ends, O opens Owner, M opens Milestone, / jumps to the line. Values can still be clicked. The keys sit behind the line's (i).
proposals.plus: No clicks at all for the common tasks once the keys are known; fastest in a meeting with the panel on screen.
proposals.cost: Add a feature 1 click; move its dates 0 clicks (E, type, Enter); set its owner 0 clicks (/ owner mira, Enter); add a milestone 0 clicks (M, type, Enter). Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. The letters and the line are new things to learn, and they do nothing on a phone.

decisions.name: Reading order and marks
decisions.question: In what order should the panel show a feature's fields, and how should a changeable and a changed field look?
decisions.common: The name on top with today's 'Code None · Not in the Ground Truth' line and a count of what needs fixing; every field editable in place (PE1 A); the fields the panel has today all kept, the rarer ones folded under More, where Notes grows as it is typed; a changed field stays marked until the panel closes; Simple's colours, type and spacing as built.

proposals.name: Grouped list, plan first
proposals.what: One list in four short groups: Plan (starts, ends, status, confidence, milestone), People (owner, decider), Goal (goal, measure, target) and Links (depends on, needed by). At rest a value has a dashed line under it; on hover it gets a box; once changed, its row gets a blue bar at the left and the value turns blue and bold.
proposals.why: Dates and owner, the things changed most in a roadmap review, come first, and the groups make the panel easier to scan than today's flat list of 20 rows. The blue bar shows what was just changed without a new word on screen.
proposals.plus: Same shape as today's panel, so it is familiar; every field always shown, nothing hidden.
proposals.cost: Add a feature 1 click; move its dates 1 click; set its owner 2 clicks; add a milestone 2 clicks (with PE1 A). Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. Longest of the three: Links can fall below the fold on a laptop.

proposals.name: Summary card first
proposals.what: A card on top holds what changes most, large: the dates as one line, then owner and status. Below it, folding sections: Goal and milestone (open), More (confidence, decider, measure; folded) and Links with their count. A changed value gets a soft blue fill.
proposals.plus: The plan reads in one glance; the panel is short until a section is opened.
proposals.cost: Add a feature 1 click; move its dates 1 click; set its owner 2 clicks; add a milestone 2 clicks (with PE1 A). Fields in a folded section (confidence, decider, measure) take 1 more click. Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. Folded fields are one more click to reach, and the panel's shape differs from the other pages' lists.

proposals.name: Two columns of tiles
proposals.what: Each field is a small tile with its label above the value, two to a row: starts and ends, owner and status, milestone and confidence, then goal across, then target and decider, then the links. A changed tile gets a blue border and a tick by its label.
proposals.plus: Short and even; each tile is a clear thing to click, and a changed one stands out.
proposals.cost: Add a feature 1 click; move its dates 1 click; set its owner 2 clicks; add a milestone 2 clicks (with PE1 A). Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. Long values wrap in a half-width tile, so rows of tiles grow uneven; boxes everywhere make the panel busier than Simple's lists.

decisions.name: Acting on a feature's flags
decisions.question: Where should a feature's flags and Oracle's suggestions be acted on in the panel?
decisions.common: Three flags on the story feature: no owner yet, Oracle's suggested dates, and a feature that needs it starting too early. Each has its fix as one-click buttons (the two people Oracle suggests or Someone else, Use these or Keep mine, Move it after or Remove link); acting clears the flag and the count at once, with Undo in the corner. A viewer sees the flags' words and no buttons; the (i) by the name says who can act. The 'Not in the Ground Truth' line stays as built, beside the code.

proposals.name: Fix on the field
proposals.what: Each flag sits under the field it is about: the owner flag under Owner with Mira Okafor and Jonah Reyes as buttons, Oracle's dates under Ends, the early start under Needed by. The count on top says how many are left.
proposals.why: The fix is shown with the value it changes, so a person sees what they are changing; one click clears it, no separate trip to Pick an owner.
proposals.plus: One click per flag; the panel keeps one reading order.
proposals.cost: Set its owner 1 click when the owner flag suggests someone; add a feature 1 click; move its dates 1 click (or Use these); add a milestone 2 clicks. Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. A flag low in the panel (links) can be below the fold; the count on top is the only sign of it.

proposals.name: List on top
proposals.what: All the flags are listed together in an amber box at the top of the panel, each with its buttons; the fields below are left plain.
proposals.plus: Everything that needs the person is in one place, first; easiest to clear in a review.
proposals.cost: Set its owner 1 click from the box; add a feature 1 click; move its dates 1 click (or Use these); add a milestone 2 clicks. Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. The fix is apart from the value it changes; with many flags the box pushes the fields down.

proposals.name: One at a time
proposals.what: The count on top is a button: it opens the first flag with its fix; acting on it brings the next one, until none are left.
proposals.plus: A calm panel until the person chooses to fix; one thing to decide at a time.
proposals.cost: Set its owner 2 clicks (the count, then the person); add a feature 1 click; move its dates 1 click; add a milestone 2 clicks. Today: add a feature 2 clicks and a drag; move its dates 3 clicks with Save; set its owner 3 clicks with Save; add a milestone 4 clicks with Save. One more click to start, and flags are easy to leave unseen.
